methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Distalmotion is a Series G robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 companies—1 public (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics—operating in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector.

A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow robotics cohort; while 10 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 met valuation-tier or stage filters required for statistical reliability. The stage-progression method is therefore the primary triangulation tool. Using total capital raised ($150M) as a valuation proxy and applying a standard Series G to next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.25x yields an implied valuation of $188M.

The triangulated range supports a median valuation of $188M, with a low of $159M (15% discount) and a high of $216M (15% premium), reflecting typical step-up variance at this stage. Key uncertainties remain: the lack of narrowly comparable late-stage robotics valuations limits confidence in peer-derived multiples, and actual revenue traction, capital efficiency, and market conditions relative to the named peer set are not quantified in this dataset. Additional diligence on recent funding terms and exit comparables would strengthen conviction in this range.
